newsitem.title: UK: New UK regulation unlikely to touch ISMA - regulator.
newsitem.headline: New UK regulation unlikely to touch ISMA - regulator.

text.p: The International Securities Market Association (ISMA) was unlikely to be affected by sweeping regulatory changes introduced by Britain, a British regulator said on Wednesday.

"ISMA is based in Switzerland and I am not sure whether the way we change the law in the UK will involve anyone from overseas," John Barrass, head of the international relations department at the Securities and Investment Board (SIB) told Reuters.
He said he was not speaking in his official SIB capacity.
In 1988 ISMA was appointed a designated investment exchange (DIE) by the SIB.
It also got approval from the British treasury as the only international securities self-regulating organisation (ISSRO) for the purposes of the 1986 Financial Services Act.

"ISMA is a unique organisation, and the government has always retained the oversight responsibility of it, unlike other self-regulatory organisations (SROs) which are SIB responsibility," Barrass said.
"The Eurobond market is a full-scale, thriving, professional market and ISMA is its recognised regulator," he said.
Shortly after coming to power in May, Britain's Labour government proposed radical changes to the country's regulatory structure.
The SIB will take over the Bank of England's banking supervision role, and three existing SROs will become part of the SIB, creating a new "Super SIB".
Barrass said the new body, which he said would not legally take on its new responsibilities until laws were changed in 1998 at the earliest, could eventually take over supervision of ISMA.
"If ISMA remains a specialised SRO then maybe the transfer of oversight will go to the SIB. That would be consistent with government plans generally," he said.
ISMA performs two roles, one as an SRO and another as an industry association for its 820 members in 51 countries.
Its main function is to facilitate a self-regulatory framework for the continued growth and development of cross-border trading in international securities.
